subject: Post-call: HelixAI evaluation runbook & scheduling
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixai.com>
Cc: KarThik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: HelixAI evaluation runbook & scheduling

Hi Alyssa / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation and helpful context on the production constraints (token caps, rate spikes during batch scoring, and data retention rules). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: quantifiable comparison vs Helix's current inference stack (in-house + cloud provider) across quality (exact-match, factuality/hallucination), latency P50/P95, and unit cost per 1K tokens.
- Deliverables we propose: evaluation runbook (prompt sets + test harness), scheduled benchmark window (we'll run parallel tests to minimize drift), and a small regression test focused on hallucination scenarios you flagged.

Concrete asks for you: please share the seed prompts/examples (for chat and single-turn scoring) and a representative sample of production inputs (anonymized) if possible — even 200 rows helps. We can run a synthetic augmentation as needed.

I attached a short prompt seed template to capture the variations you called out. Please drop the file back to me or upload to the Drive link we shared during the call.

Proposed timeline (rapid):
1) You send seed prompts + one-week access window preference by Wed 18 Mar.
2) Redwood runs parallel benchmarks Thurs–Fri 19–20 Mar (short runs to validate, extended run on request).
3) We share an initial results snapshot and recording by Mon 23 Mar, plus a suggested follow-up test matrix.

I'll coordinate with KarThik and Grace on the runbook and will include our regression checks for hallucination rate by prompt category.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: eval_seed_template.txt (text)]

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: HelixAI evaluation runbook & scheduling

Thanks, Priyom — great summary.

Attached: customer_eval_seed_prompts.txt (we redacted PII). I've included three categories: customer support transcripts, product spec Q&A, and code-assist snippets. A couple notes:
- Our current infra uses a mix of open models + AWS Bedrock endpoints for scale.
- The biggest pain is hallucination on product specs and inconsistent token accounting (cost spikes on long conversations).

Quick clarifying Qs:
1) Will you run the same prompt order for all systems (we want apples-to-apples)?
2) Can you include a short hallucination-specific prompt set (we flagged 12 examples) to see false-positives?
3) Any limits on our side for test windows or IP sharing requirements?

Tom (cc'd) will help surface the sample rows from our analytics bucket; we may need an NDA addendum for the raw logs — is your standard SOC2 addendum sufficient?

If the above timeline works, we'd prefer the benchmarks to run Thu 19 Mar so our engineers can shadow the runs.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Head of ML Ops
HelixAI
[Attachment: customer_eval_seed_prompts.txt (text)]

From: KarThik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@helixai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: HelixAI evaluation runbook & scheduling

Hi all — thanks for the prompt seeds, Alyssa. I pulled a quick proposed test plan into the attached runbook and test matrix. Highlights: 

- Test methodology: deterministic ordering (seeded RNG), identical prompt context across endpoints, and tokenization-normalized cost calc so we avoid double-counting.
- Systems to include: Helix in-house model (v2), AWS Bedrock endpoint(s) they currently hit, and two Redwood-configured variants (open quantized and a Redwood-optimized fp16 variant).
- Metrics we will report: exact-match for canned Q&A, hallucination rate (we'll annotate false facts), P50/P95 latency (cold vs warmed cache), tokens per response, and relative unit cost normalized to Helix baseline.
- Regression checks: a 12-item hallucination pack (you included) will be run at 3 different temperatures; we'll flag any >10% false-positive rate.

Attached files: redwood_eval_plan_v1.md, test_matrix.csv. We'll also produce a small JSON with regression baseline results (redwood_regression_benchmarks_v0.json) after the first short run.

Operational notes: we can run the short parallel sweep Thu 19 Mar starting 09:00 PST and finish by 14:00 PST if your team is available. No additional IP paperwork required beyond the standard SOC2 addendum — Priyom will share that.

Next immediate action: Alyssa to confirm sample rows upload or transfer mechanism by EOD Wed 18 Mar.

Thanks,
KarThik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood_eval_plan_v1.md (markdown), test_matrix.csv (csv)]

Link: https://hubspot.com/contacts/DEAL-4392 (internal)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_sample

Tom/Alyssa — if that window works, I'll send a calendar invite and a short run checklist.

Thanks,
Priyom

Thanks, Priyom — that window works for us.

I've asked infra to stage a sanitized sample export to the Drive link (should arrive by 10:30 PST). We'll have one of our engineers shadow the run and join the call at 09:00 PST to watch for cost anomalies.

One ask before the run: can Redwood include a quick side-by-side of tokenization differences between systems (just a short appendix) so we can validate the normalization? That will be critical for our finance and SRE reviews.

Appreciate it — Tom
Director, ML Infrastructure
HelixAI
